books.title: The Lighthouse Keeper
books.content:
The lamp had not been lit for three nights, and old Maren felt the silence
press against the glass like a tide. She climbed the spiral stair with the
oil can knocking at her knee, counting the steps she had counted ten thousand
times before the storms took her hearing.

On the fourth night a green flare cut the fog above the reef. Maren answered
with two long flashes and one short, the old wartime code, and waited to see
whether anyone still living remembered how to read the dark.

books.title: On Reading Fast
books.content:
Most people read at the pace they learned to speak, sounding each word in the
throat even when the page is silent. This book is about letting that habit go.

The inner voice is a comfortable bottleneck. It caps you near speaking speed,
a few hundred words a minute, long after your eyes could move faster.

Widen the span. Let groups of words land at once, trust the periphery, and
resist the pull back to the safe, slow line you already understood.
